rows.title: NFL wind: four Sunday totals to verify
rows.observation: The November 1 source selections are NE–MIA under 43.5 (-113), LAC–LAR under 45.5 (-111), ATL–TB under 43.5 (-111), and IND–JAX under 46.5 (-110). The screen uses average wind of at least 10 mph and temperatures from 33 to 90 degrees; displayed history is 635-467-10 with 11% ROI.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: these are source claims, not verified game-time weather effects. Stadium shelter and roof conditions can invalidate an outdoor weather proxy. Historical ROI is not a forecast for these four games.
rows.next_check: Verify venue, roof/open-air exposure and forecast near kickoff; compare the exact current total and price. Re-capture tomorrow before a new decision. No automatic wind adjustment.
rows.quote_status: Source-pick benchmark only; no verified executable sportsbook quote

rows.title: Portland–Utah: investigate the under
rows.observation: Action lists Under 232.5 at -112 as a system selection for October 31. Its displayed history is 534 wins, 434 losses, 9 pushes and 7% ROI. Filters include division games in the regular season, under support at 40% or less, and a total falling by at least one point from open to close.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: closing-line information is unavailable when an earlier ticket is placed. This is a third-party historical screen, not our calibrated win probability. The discovery row and expanded chart also disagree on total units; those units are not used.
rows.next_check: Compare the same sportsbook total at the actual decision time, verify line movement and current injuries/pace, then track an independent forward benchmark. Do not apply a fixed probability boost or copy the source stake.

rows.title: System discovery: win rate alone can mislead
rows.observation: The catalog includes both winning and losing historical screens. Its college-football Sharp Money screen shows 51% wins and -1% ROI; an MLB public-fade moneyline screen shows 59% wins and -3% ROI.
rows.interpretation: Use price-adjusted returns, sample size and forward results; neither a sharp-money label nor a high hit rate proves value. Selecting only the best historical screens risks selection bias.
rows.next_check: Keep source systems separate from agency results; test rules prospectively with timestamped inputs and realistic prices before changing betting behavior.
rows.quote_status: Source-pick benchmark only; no verified executable sportsbook quote

rows.title: College football: compare external model disagreements
rows.observation: At capture the dashboard displayed South Alabama +6.5 versus projection +2, Air Force +0.5 versus -3.5, and Kansas State +2.5 versus -1.2 for October 31 matchups. These are external model comparison leads, not accepted picks or verified book offers.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: a forecast disagreement identifies something to investigate. It does not establish which model is right. The dashboard supplies no named executable sportsbook for these displayed offers.
rows.next_check: Resolve full team/event identities and current sportsbook contracts, compare our forecast and injuries, and preserve the disagreement for later outcome scoring.

used.reason: Colorado Buffaloes offense +0.126 (9 games) vs Cincinnati Bearcats defense allowed +0.278 (9 games); Cincinnati Bearcats offense +0.208 (9 games) vs Colorado Buffaloes defense allowed +0.082 (9 games); CFBD PPA Colorado Buffaloes: offense +0.039 (9 games), defense allowed +0.116 (9 games); CFBD PPA Cincinnati Bearcats: offense +0.169 (9 games), defense allowed +0.248 (9 games). The existing CFB spread forecast already uses opponent-adjusted EPA alongside other metrics; do not add these descriptive averages to its probability again. Passing/rushing are context, not a separately validated matchup edge. Missing values mean unknown. Check sample, opponent strength, injuries and pace; EPA alone is not a spread, total, player projection or bet instruction. Verified AI caution/reject assessments can tighten or hold a decision; narrative summaries cannot set probabilities. These hypotheses are not proven profitable. Counterpoint keeps its separate inverse experiment; NFL prop holds remain.
limitations: No unattended Action Network collection; snapshots expire after 30 minutes

Existing tickets are never reselected or rewritten

decision_policy.note: Active experimental paper rule: for moneylines and spreads laying points (including pick-em), if the selected team has at least 0.05 lower offensive PPA/play AND at least 0.05 higher defensive PPA allowed than its opponent, require 2 additional percentage points of model edge and cap the stake at one unit. All four overall samples need at least four games and fresh, matched CFBD evidence. Totals, underdog spreads, missing/stale samples and mixed evidence retain existing rules. This is an unvalidated selection screen, not a calibrated probability model. Counterpoint keeps its inverse experiment.

claude_reviews.summary: Top observations (static review of excerpts only; I did not run code, and saved tests cover a different snapshot so they do not certify this code). 1) Definite stale-state bug: shared_research_service.py line 105 returns 'cached' for 30 minutes after any run, but report state is stored only at line 150 after deliver(). A mid-window refresh of saved inputs (new hypotheses, briefings, market snapshots) is not delivered until the next window, and force=False callers get no staleness signal. Also, deliveries are keyed by digest of content (line 92) that omits 'now', so INSERT OR IGNORE silently dedupes unchanged content while evaluate() results depend on time-based expiry (lines 25-26); an agency whose decisions flip from SHADOW_CANDIDATE to WATCH due to expiry but whose counts happen to repeat an earlier digest will not be re-recorded. Hypothesis (needs validation): digest collision across time windows. 2) Temporal-leakage risk in information_intake.py: candidate() (lines 119-128) checks p['expired'] computed at load() time, not at decision time, so a long-lived rows list can mark stale inputs eligible; also native() line 78 caps expiry with tip_utc but moneyline branch line 84 does not cap when tip_utc is missing (end=created, so expired immediately, which is safe but unintended). For external rows (line 65) 'target' is {} so candidates are labeled sport_context_only; correct, but the evaluate() path in shared_research_service never consults candidate() constraints, meaning NBA hypotheses can reach SHADOW_CANDIDATE (line 32) without the intake/adapter freshness gate being recomputed at the decision time of that call; only evidence ages in lines 25-26 are rechecked. 3) Identity/integrity: read_briefings (lines 34-56) validates evidence_ids against 'known' built from rows regardless of expiry (lines 64-77), so a briefing can reference expired or future-tip-passed evidence, and assessments() in information_intake.py (line 98) trusts any briefing with automatic_api_call true and assessment_version match; it relies on verified_briefing() (not supplied) for authenticity, so that receipt check is unverified here. Minor: information_intake.validate does not check captured_utc is not in the future relative to now, and the credential regex (line 27) only catches sk- style keys. No bankroll or wager accounting changes are present in these excerpts.

Top observations (hypotheses/validation gaps unless noted; I did not run code): (1) Temporal gating is by week number only. cfb_efficiency.py lines 80-81 and cfbd_ppa.py line 117 use week < before_week plus an unvalidated kickoff check, so bye weeks, postseason weeks, or mislabeled week fields could admit or omit games, and cfbd_ppa.attach never rechecks kickoff against tip_utc (line 117 vs line 108). Also cfb_efficiency.py line 63 and cfbd_ppa.py line 108 use a 6-hour finality buffer while the CSV freshness only requires file mtime within 24h, so a CSV could include games finished after saved_utc without being flagged; line 109 mtime is the sole snapshot timestamp. (2) Identity/matching risk in cfbd_ppa.py lines 89-93 and 111: school() uses longest normalized prefix of the full team name, so 'Miami (OH)' vs 'Miami', 'Southern Miss', or mascot-suffixed names may resolve wrongly or collide; both teams must match the pair, which mitigates but the guard is only a hypothesis-level safeguard without test data. Duplicate gameId handling at lines 100-106 silently drops entries rather than failing loudly. cfbd_ppa.fetch line 44 returns 'already_reserved' with empty rows after an interrupted request, yielding a stale reservation that blocks recapture for the whole UTC day (definite availability defect, safe fail-closed). (3) Policy/calibration: cfb_efficiency.py lines 206-207 apply a 2pp edge increase and the docstring claims a one-unit stake cap, but apply_policy only raises out['threshold']; no cap on stake is enforced in the supplied code (line 207-213), so the cap relies on unseen downstream handling. The 0.05 thresholds and 2pp are uncalibrated, correlated with the model's own EPA inputs (potential double-adjustment, though probability is unchanged), and test evidence is for a different snapshot, so tests do not certify this.

1) ai_budget.py:42-44: spend() counts every reserved/uncertain row regardless of period, but the same filter ignores day/provider scoping only via the status clause, so a stale uncertain row inflates daily, provider and monthly totals indefinitely (intentional carry-forward, but it also makes day-scoped limits unreachable until manual reconciliation; there is no reconcile path in the supplied code). Definite design risk, not a crash. 2) ai_research_worker.py:263-264 plus ai_budget.py:90-91: main() marks every 'reserved' row uncertain at startup, but the lock is acquired in the same process so concurrent live calls are not an issue; however ai_budget.py:65 then blocks all paid calls for both providers on any uncertain row, and nothing in the supplied files clears it, so one crash or timeout can permanently halt the service (unverified: a reconcile tool may exist elsewhere). 3) ai_research_worker.py:113 vs :182: review dedupe checks digest([model,candidate]) in attempted, but run_one stores job_key=digest([model,packet.get('review_key',packet)]) which hashes the review_key string alone, not [model,candidate]-style list of the key; these are different digests only if review_key is a plain string passed as digest([MODELS,review_key]) -- they match in form, but the retry path (:272-282) replays the saved packet and the cost reserve uses len(system+content), fine; the remaining concern is ai_budget.py:67 cooldown comparing now to stored started_utc without tz validation, and ai_research_worker.py:146 uses an unusual thinking type 'between_tools' (hypothesis: possible invalid API param causing 400s). Validation receipt is stale, so no test evidence supports approval.

events.detail: Top observations (hypotheses/validation gaps unless noted; I did not run code): (1) Temporal gating is by week number only. cfb_efficiency.py lines 80-81 and cfbd_ppa.py line 117 use week < before_week plus an unvalidated kickoff check, so bye weeks, postseason weeks, or mislabeled week fields could admit or omit games, and cfbd_ppa.attach never rechecks kickoff against tip_utc (line 117 vs line 108). Also cfb_efficiency.py line 63 and cfbd_ppa.py line 108 use a 6-hour finality buffer while the CSV freshness only requires file mtime within 24h, so a CSV could include games finished after saved_utc without being flagged; line 109 mtime is the sole snapshot timestamp. (2) Identity/matching risk in cfbd_ppa.py lines 89-93 and 111: school() uses longest normalized prefix of the full team name, so 'Miami (OH)' vs 'Miami', 'Southern Miss', or mascot-suffixed names may resolve wrongly or collide; both teams must match the pair, which mitigates but the guard is only a hypothesis-level safeguard without test data. Duplicate gameId handling at lines 100-106 silently drops entries rather than failing loudly. cfbd_ppa.fetch line 44 returns 'already_reserved' with empty rows after an interrupted request, yielding a stale reservation that blocks recapture for the whole UTC day (definite availability defect, safe fail-closed). (3) Policy/calibration: cfb_efficiency.py lines 206-207 apply a 2pp edge increase and the docstring claims a one-unit stake cap, but apply_policy only raises out['threshold']; no cap on stake is enforced in the supplied code (line 207-213), so the cap relies on unseen downstream handling. The 0.05 thresholds and 2pp are uncalibrated, correlated with the model's own EPA inputs (potential double-adjustment, though probability is unchanged), and test evidence is for a different snapshot, so tests do not certify this.

bankroll_policy: New paper stakes: at most 40% committed overall, 10% per sport, 2% per game and 1% per ticket. At most 10% committed beyond 24 hours. Sportsbook NBA/NFL game lines may use 7.5% per sport, leaving 2.5% of bankroll for props within the 10% sport limit. Percentages use the lower of initial bankroll and current cash plus open stakes; profits do not automatically increase limits. Existing locked tickets remain intact, and may exceed new limits until settlement. Model and sportsbook accounts stay separate.
